Article Title: IPL investment later, The Hundred continues to be a family affair
Article Text:
Matthew Potts of SunRisers Leeds reacts after MI London won the Hundred Men's match between MI London and SunRisers Leeds at The Kia Oval on July 21, 2026 in London, England.

TimesofIndia.com in London:

The summer of cricket continues unabated in England. The men played three Tests against New Zealand and five T20Is and three ODIs against India. As for the women, there was the T20 World Cup and the one-off Test between India and England. And now, it is the turn of The Hundred, which began on July 21.The Hundred, the unique tournament featuring 100-ball innings, is back with its sixth edition. Much has changed, and yet not a lot has changed. It still has eight teams, still features 100-ball innings where bowlers can bowl spells of five or 10 consecutive balls, and is still objectively meant to quicken the game and feature double headers - men and women - on the same day.On the opening day, defending men's champions MI London beat Sunrisers Leeds at The Oval. In the day's first game, Sunrisers edged MI London by 7 wickets in the women's competition. A day later, in Southampton, Southern Brave women narrowly got the better of Welsh Fire. And the men's match later in the day had the reverse outcome.What's changed is the ownership, the team names, and the kit designs. After an influx of £520 million into The Hundred, the Ambani family acquired Oval Invincibles (now renamed MI London), Sun Group purchased Northern Superchargers (now SunRisers Leeds), and RPSG Group bought Manchester Originals (now Manchester Super Giants).GMR Group, co-owners of the Delhi Capitals, have taken a 49% stake in Southern Brave.On the opening day of the season at The Oval, the mood was as relaxed as one would expect at this time of year. The sun was out, and it was a pleasant day, away from the baking heat that this country had seen in the last couple of months. Even though it was a weekday, families were out in numbers, making the most of numerous entry points that get you into this cricket stadium in Kennington.A venue that has seen three consecutive Test defeats for the hosts. It was here just a month ago that New Zealand walloped England by 253 runs. And it was here just about a year ago that Mohammed Siraj bowled with great fire to help India secure a series-levelling win by just 6 runs.But now, on a Tuesday, The Hundred got underway, and the buzz was equal parts cricket, family and entertainment. A father, holding the hands of two of his kids, walked around and sought the support of a steward in finding the “family section.” Unlike international cricket, where tickets get sold for £100 or more, The Hundred hopes to bring in the masses with reasonable pricing.With kids two and under going free, tickets for 3-15-year-olds are worth £5, and tickets for adults start from as little as £14. So, an entire young family could see two consecutive cricket matches, spanning about five hours or over, for £30-40.To unwind after a long day at work, numerous food carts, kiosks and drinks stalls came to the rescue. From Middle Eastern to fast food to Indian, everything was on offer to suit the palates of the patrons. To glug it down are a range of soft drinks, beers, cocktails and other non-alcoholic beverages. Most importantly, perhaps, ice creams in different flavours and styles are just what the youngsters ask for.The difference in atmosphere quality between the Indian Premier League, a mature cricket league, and The Hundred, still finding its feet, is huge. Now that there is investment by IPL franchises and Indian conglomerates into The Hundred, its way is only forward, helped in large part by a family-oriented approach.
Article Summary: The Hundred, the unique tournament featuring 100-ball innings, is back with its sixth edition. On the opening day, defending men's champions MI London beat Sunrisers Leeds at The Oval. In the day's first game, SunRisers edged MI London by 7 wickets in the women's competition. A day later, in Southampton, Southern Brave women narrowly got the better of Welsh Fire. And the men's match later in the day had the reverse outcome.

NEW DELHI: The 2026 Commonwealth Games begin on Thursday in Glasgow, Scotland. However, fans will notice that several popular sports, including cricket. Apart from cricket, hockey, badminton and wrestling, are also missing from this year's programme.The number of sports has been reduced from 19 at the 2022 Birmingham Games to just 10 in Glasgow. The decision has also affected India's medal hopes, as many of the country's strongest events have been dropped.Cricket was dropped from the Glasgow Games mainly because of financial and logistical reasons.The 2026 Commonwealth Games were originally awarded to Victoria, Australia. However, the state government withdrew as host in 2023 because of rising costs. Glasgow was later confirmed as the replacement host in September 2024, leaving organisers with limited time to prepare.To keep the Games affordable and sustainable, organisers reduced the number of sports from 19 to 10.Yes. Cricket made its Commonwealth Games debut at the 1998 Kuala Lumpur Games.The competition featured only the men's ODI format, with 16 teams taking part. South Africa, led by Shaun Pollock, won the gold medal after defeating Australia in the final.New Zealand claimed the bronze medal by beating Sri Lanka.The West Indies were represented by three separate teams — Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados and Jamaica. India also sent a split national team, while Scotland and Northern Ireland represented the British Isles.Cricket returned after a gap of 24 years at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games, this time as a women's T20 tournament with eight teams.Australia, captained by Meg Lanning, won the gold medal. India finished with silver, while New Zealand secured the bronze.Nine sports from Birmingham 2022 have been removed from the Glasgow programme:The decision is a major setback for India. India finished fourth at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games with 61 medals. Half of those medals came in sports that are no longer part of the Games.These six sports alone contributed 30 medals to India's overall tally. Shooting and archery, two other events where India has traditionally performed well, were already missing from the programme.
Article Summary: Cricket made its Commonwealth Games debut at the 1998 Kuala Lumpur Games. The number of sports has been reduced from 19 at the 2022 Birmingham Games to just 10 in Glasgow. The decision is a major setback for India, as many of the country's strongest events have been dropped.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.
Article Summary: India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two- week multinational training camp in Belfast. The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp. Article Title: Relief for Lalit Modi as tribunal quashes 2009 ED penalty
Article Text:
Lalit Modi

Former IPL chairman Lalit Modi , the BCCI and some of its office-bearers received major relief after the Appellate Tribunal under SAFEMA set aside a key Enforcement Directorate (ED) penalty in a Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) case linked to the 2009 Indian Premier League in South Africa.The case stemmed from the IPL’s relocation to South Africa due to India’s general elections in 2009. The ED had alleged that overseas remittances of around 243 crore ($49.86 million) made to Cricket South Africa for hosting the tournament violated FEMA provisions.However, a division bench comprising chairman Justice Munishwar Nath Bhandari and member Rajesh Malhotra ruled that the payments were legitimate operational expenses and qualified as current account transactions, which did not require prior approval from the Reserve Bank of India. The judgment was delivered on July 16.In its order, the tribunal described Modi as the “chief architect” behind the organisation of IPL-2 in South Africa and held that there was no material to show he was responsible for BCCI’s statutory FEMA compliance. It termed the penalty imposed on him “wholly erroneous” and set it aside.Welcoming the verdict, Modi said: “The Tribunal has rejected the central premise on which the Enforcement Directorate’s case against me had been built.It held that the principal foreign remittances relating to IPL 2009 in South Africa were current account transactions, not capital account transactions.”Calling the ruling a vindication after a prolonged legal battle, Modi added: “For over 16 years I have consistently maintained that I acted in good faith, in the best interests of Indian cricket and the IPL, and committed no personal wrongdoing.”The tribunal also granted relief to the BCCI and State Bank of India, overturning most of the ED’s 2018 penalty order while retaining only minor fines on the BCCI for administrative delays.
Article Summary: Former IPL chairman Lalit Modi and the BCCI receive major relief. The Appellate Tribunal under SAFEMA set aside a key Enforcement Directorate penalty. The case stemmed from the IPL's relocation to South Africa due to India's general elections in 2009.

Article Title: Bangladesh pacer Taskin Ahmed pulls out of LPL 2026 to prepare for Australia Test tour
Article Text:
Bangladesh's Taskin Ahmed (PTI Photo)

Taskin prioritises Test preparations over franchise cricket



Bangladesh eye historic Australia tour





Bangladesh pacer Taskin Ahmed has withdrawn from the Lanka Premier League (LPL) 2026 to prioritise preparations for the upcoming two-match Test series against Australia in August.Taskin was set to represent Jaffna Kings in the LPL after receiving a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB). However, the fast bowler has opted out of the tournament to focus on Bangladesh's historic Test tour of Australia, where they will play a two-match series Down Under for the first time since 2003.The right-arm pacer had initially planned to skip the T20I series against Zimbabwe and travel to Sri Lanka for the LPL. However, he remained with the Bangladesh squad after Mustafizur Rahman was ruled out due to injury. Explaining his decision, Taskin said the Australia series, which is part of the ongoing ICC World Test Championship cycle, was too important to compromise his preparations."Yeah, I had withdrawn myself from the LPL and it is mainly for Australia Test series preparation," Taskin told Cricbuzz."We played six back-to-back matches in Zimbabwe. Maybe I would have got four matches there (in the LPL). After my stint there, if I returned home and immediately went to Australia, my Test match preparation would have been hampered," he added.Bangladesh are scheduled to play the first Test in Darwin from August 13 to 17, while the second Test will be held in Mackay from August 22 to 26. Despite acknowledging the financial sacrifice involved in pulling out of the franchise league, Taskin insisted that representing Bangladesh in Australia took precedence."Despite a little loss, I thought it's okay because an Australia Test series won't come around often. That's why I took the decision and pulled out of the LPL even after having the NOC," he said.
Article Summary: Bangladesh pacer Taskin Ahmed has withdrawn from the Lanka Premier League (LPL) 2026. Taskin was set to represent Jaffna Kings in the LPL after receiving a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) The fast bowler has opted out of the tournament to focus on Bangladesh's historic Test tour of Australia.

Article Title: 'He must have rectified where he went wrong': Shreyas Iyer backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ahead of Zimbabwe series
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Shreyas Iyer (ANI Photos)

Iyer urges fearless cricket



Sooryavanshi ready to move on



NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer has thrown his weight behind teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ahead of the three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe, expressing confidence that the youngster has learned from his difficult introduction to international cricket and is ready to make a stronger impact.Speaking on the eve of the series opener in Harare, Iyer said he had no concerns about Sooryavanshi's ability to bounce back after the 15-year-old endured a challenging tour of England.The teenager, who became India's youngest-ever international cricketer during the England series, managed only modest returns before being left out of the fifth match as Sanju Samson returned to the playing XI.Despite the setback, Iyer believes the youngster has used the break productively."All the youngsters, I think, they have definitely practiced. There was a decent gap after the T20 series. So he (Sooryavanshi) must have rectified where he went wrong. So personally, I don't have to give much advice," Iyer said.India head into the Zimbabwe series looking to recover from a disappointing white-ball tour of Ireland and England under Iyer's captaincy.The skipper urged his young squad to play with freedom rather than worrying about criticism or the fear of failure."I don't think they should fear failure because when you have such thoughts at the back of your mind, then you play to save yourself. When you don't have that fear, you can get the best out of yourself," Iyer had said.With India travelling directly from England and having only one practice session before the opening match, Iyer acknowledged the challenge but backed his side to adapt quickly.Reflecting on his own comeback from injury, the 31-year-old said overcoming setbacks had made him mentally stronger."It has made me more confident as an individual. When you overcome the injury phase, mentally it makes you very positive. Whatever challenges you face on the field, you know how quickly you can overcome them," he said.Sooryavanshi, meanwhile, admitted that the last four months have been an emotional rollercoaster but insisted his confidence remains intact."Yes, there have been several ups and down in the last four months; it's part of cricket it will keep happening but I have to follow the process and give my 100 per cent for the team," the youngster told bcci .tv.His omission from the final T20I against England had sparked criticism of the team management, with several former cricketers questioning the decision to drop the teenager after just three innings.However, Sooryavanshi said the support from the coaching staff helped him regain his focus."It's an obvious thing that whatever I want (guidance etc), the coaches are making it available and whatever practice I require I am getting that. Feeling very good, there is confidence also," he said.The Zimbabwe tour also carries special significance for the youngster. It was at the same venue in Harare that he starred in India's triumphant Under-19 World Cup campaign earlier this year, smashing a breathtaking 175 off just 80 balls against England in the final."It's a very memorable ground for me. Just four months back, we had played the U-19 World Cup Final and won, so a very special ground," he said.Confident of the knowledge he gained during that tournament, Sooryavanshi said he hopes to use his familiarity with the conditions if selected for the opening T20I."I will back my practice which I have done so far and try to back my game... whatever contribution I can make for the team I will try to give that," he said.
Article Summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer has thrown his weight behind teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ahead of the three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe. The teenager became India's youngest-ever international cricketer during the England series. India head into the series looking to recover from a disappointing white-ball tour of Ireland and England under Iyer's captaincy.

'KL Rahul is at par with Virat Kohli in talent'



Virat Kohli vs KL Rahul: International career comparison



Stat Virat Kohli KL Rahul International Matches 562 238 Runs 28,359 9,830 Batting Average 52.71 40.45 Centuries 85 22 Half-centuries 148 62 Highest Score 254* 199

Former India opener Wasim Jaffer has made a bold comparison between KL Rahul and Virat Kohli , saying the Indian wicketkeeper-batter possesses the same level of talent and technical ability as the batting great. However, Jaffer believes it is Kohli's unmatched mentality and relentless consistency that have helped him scale unprecedented heights in international cricket.Rahul and Kohli have shared the Indian dressing room for over a decade, with the duo making their international careers around the same era. While Kohli has gone on to become one of the greatest batters of the modern era, Rahul has often been praised for his elegant strokeplay and versatility but has struggled to convert his immense potential into sustained dominance.Speaking on The Great Indian Cricket Show on Doordarshan, Jaffer reflected on his time as part of the Punjab Kings coaching setup and recalled working closely with Rahul during the IPL.Jaffer described Rahul as one of the most technically complete batters in world cricket and said the Karnataka star still has plenty to achieve."KL is a top-class player who plays all three formats remarkably well. Technically sound, composed, and level-headed.Even though he is still actively playing, I believe he has somewhat underachieved given his skill set. He can get so many more runs for both India and his franchise," Jaffer said.The former India opener then made a striking comparison with Kohli."In terms of pure talent and quality, I genuinely believe he is at par with Virat Kohli, but it is Virat's elite mentality that creates that ultimate separation between KL and Virat," he added.Although Jaffer rates Rahul's talent alongside Kohli's, the numbers underline the remarkable gap created by Kohli's longevity and consistency as Kohli started his international career 6 years prior to KL Rahul.
Article Summary: Former India opener Wasim Jaffer has made a bold comparison between KL Rahul and Virat Kohli. Jaffer believes the Indian wicketkeeper-batter possesses the same level of talent and technical ability as the batting great. The former India opener believes it is Kohli's unmatched mentality and relentless consistency that have helped him scale unprecedented heights in international cricket.

Article Title: 'There were a lot of positives': Shreyas Iyer reflects on 'rough' England tour, urges fearless approach in Zimbabwe
Article Text:
India skipper Shreyas Iyer during a T20I match against England. (ANI Photo)

'Don't fear failure'



Quick turnaround, fresh challenge



NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer believes his team's disappointing white-ball tour of England and Ireland has laid the foundation for future success, insisting the difficult phase has brought the squad closer together ahead of the three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe.After enduring a winless campaign in England and Ireland in what was Iyer's first assignment as India's T20I captain, the visitors will now look to turn the page when they face Zimbabwe in the opening T20I on Thursday.Rather than dwelling on the setbacks, Iyer said the challenging tour offered valuable lessons about the team's mindset, adaptability and decision-making under pressure."We had a rough patch in England, but there were a lot of positives out of that. We got to know what we have to build as a team going forward, what kind of presence of mind, awareness and adaptability we need once we step onto the field," Iyer said on the eve of the series opener.With India looking to bounce back immediately, Iyer urged his young squad to embrace an attacking mindset instead of worrying about criticism or the fear of failure."I don't think they should fear failure because when you have such thoughts at the back of your mind, then you play to save yourself.When you don't have that fear, you can get the best out of yourself," the skipper said."We don't have to think much about what people are saying outside. We have to stay in the present. The more we play good cricket and play together as a unit, the better it will be for the team," he added.The captain added that the difficult results had only strengthened the bond within the dressing room."The results didn't go our way, but that has brought the team closer to each other. We've been having a lot of discussions about how we're going to play as a unit going forward. It's a great exposure because you don't get this often. This is a challenging phase, and the quicker you overcome it, the better you become as a team," Iyer said.India have had little time to regroup after travelling directly from England, with only one practice session before the opening match in Zimbabwe.Calling the schedule demanding but exciting, Iyer backed his team to adapt quickly to unfamiliar conditions."It is definitely very challenging. We came yesterday, today is practice and tomorrow is the match. But it is fun, and if you perform well in these situations, you will definitely be happy with yourself," the new captain said.The 31-year-old, touring Zimbabwe for the first time, acknowledged that adjusting quickly would be crucial."Some of us are playing here for the first time, so the quicker we adapt, the better results we will get," he added.Iyer also warned against underestimating Zimbabwe, praising the hosts for having an experienced squad with several players who have featured in the IPL."They have an amazing team and a good lineup. A couple of them have also played in the IPL, so they carry immense experience," he said.
Article Summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer says tour of England and Ireland has laid the foundation for future success. The 31-year-old says the difficult phase has brought the squad closer together ahead of the three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe. Iyer urges his young squad to embrace an attacking mindset instead of worrying about criticism or fear of failure.

Article Title: 'He was struggling': Former India cricketer slams Shubman Gill's captaincy against England
Article Text:
Shubman Gill and Gurnoor Brar during 3rd ODI against England, at Lord's in London on Sunday. (ANI Photo)

Hanuma Vihari questions Gill's bowling management



Vihari puzzled by Kuldeep Yadav's omission



Former India batter Hanuma Vihari has questioned Shubman Gill's captaincy following India's 27-run defeat to England in the third ODI at Lord's, criticizing the team's decision to field only five bowling options in the series decider.India suffered a heartbreaking defeat as England posted a record-breaking 387/3, the highest ODI total at Lord's, before the visitors fell short despite Rohit Sharma's brilliant century. With Jasprit Bumrah ruled out due to a knee injury, India entered the match with four specialist pacers and Axar Patel as the lone spinner, leaving Gill without a sixth bowling option. The inexperienced attack struggled to contain England's batters, with Ben Duckett's 141 and Jacob Bethell's 91 powering the hosts to a daunting total.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Vihari felt Gill struggled to rotate his bowlers because of the lack of an additional bowling option."Having just five bowlers in the last ODI, he (Gill) was struggling with his bowling changes. When everyone was getting hit, not having a sixth option became a concern for him, You should also know how to handle things when this option is not there. Whether it is field placement or bowling changes, I feel he has to improve.He has a lot to improve in captaincy. His batting is outstanding, but he has to get better as captain because the results are not coming," Hanuma Vihari said.Vihari also questioned the decision to leave wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav out of the playing XI, arguing that India should prioritize experienced match-winners in the build-up to the ODI World Cup."Why was Kuldeep left out? It is something that I cannot understand. Going with youth in T20s is still fine, but in ODIs you have to go with experience. Seeing the IPL, you feel there are many new players, but match-winners are very few, and you have to pick those match-winners. If winning the World Cup is your goal, you have to back experienced players and those who know how to win games," Vihari concluded.This was India's first ODI series loss against England since 2018.
Article Summary: Hanuma Vihari questions Shubman Gill's captaincy following India's 27-run defeat to England in the third ODI at Lord's. The former India batter also questioned the team's decision to field only five bowling options in the series decider. India entered the match with four specialist pacers and Axar Patel as the lone spinner.

Article Title: Rahmat Shah named Afghanistan captain after Hashmatullah Shahidi resigns; Gurbaaz named deputy
Article Text:
Rahmat Shah and Rahmanullah Gurbaz (Image: Agencies / PTI)

Hashmatullah Shahidi's successful captaincy

Historic bilateral success under Shahidi



Following the resignation of long-serving captain Hashmatullah Shahidi, the Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) has announced a new leadership group for the national team's Test and ODI sides.Veteran batter Rahmat Shah has been appointed as Afghanistan's new Test and ODI captain, while wicketkeeper-batter Rahmanullah Gurbaz will serve as vice-captain in both formats. The duo will officially begin their leadership roles during Afghanistan's upcoming series against Ireland.Shahidi's tenure as captain began on May 31, 2021, and he enjoyed one of the most successful leadership spells in Afghanistan's cricket history. He started his captaincy with an ODI series victory over the Netherlands in January 2022 and went on to lead Afghanistan to 27 wins in 55 ODIs.One of the biggest highlights of Shahidi's captaincy came at the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023, where Afghanistan stunned several cricketing giants by defeating England, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and the Netherlands to finish sixth in the tournament.That memorable campaign secured Afghanistan's qualification for the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, where the team made history on its tournament debut by defeating England and eventually finishing fifth overall.Under Shahidi's leadership, Afghanistan also reached their highest-ever position of seventh in the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings, another landmark achievement for the nation.Afghanistan enjoyed unprecedented success in ODI cricket during Shahidi's tenure. The team won five consecutive ODI series between 2024 and 2025 against Ireland, South Africa, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe and Bangladesh. The series triumph over South Africa was particularly significant as it marked Afghanistan's first-ever bilateral ODI series victory over the Proteas.Shahidi also guided Afghanistan to three successive ODI series wins over Bangladesh, beginning with an away triumph in 2023 before following it up with back-to-back series victories in the UAE in 2024 and 2025.In a statement, the Afghanistan Cricket Board thanked Shahidi for his outstanding service, dedication, and leadership, while wishing him success in the next phase of his career.Explaining Rahmat Shah's appointment, the ACB highlighted that he has served as Afghanistan's vice-captain in both Tests and ODIs since 2021. With vast international experience and a deep understanding of the team's structure, the board believes he is well-equipped to lead Afghanistan into a new era. The board also expressed confidence that Rahmanullah Gurbaz, as vice-captain, will complement Rahmat's leadership and help the team achieve further success.Meanwhile, Ibrahim Zadran continues as Afghanistan's T20I captain after taking over the role from Rashid Khan in March 2026, meaning Afghanistan will now have separate captains across formats.
Article Summary: Rahmat Shah appointed as Afghanistan's new Test and ODI captain. Wicketkeeper- batter Rahmanullah Gurbaz will serve as vice-captain in both formats. Long- serving captain Hashmatullah Shahidi has resigned from the role. Ibrahim Zadran will continue to be Afghanistan's T20 captain.

Article Title: 'No one has ever done this before': Harbhajan Singh makes massive Vaibhav Sooryavanshi claim
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Rahul Dravid 's question and Sooryavanshi's unforgettable answer



Tendulkar's advice that shaped Harbhajan's career



Former India spinner Harbhajan Singh has showered praise on teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, calling him an "unbelievable" talent and claiming the youngster is achieving something "no one has ever done before" with his fearless approach to the game.Speaking on JioStar, Harbhajan said Sooryavanshi's confidence and willingness to back his instincts represent the changing mindset of modern-day cricketers, who are now encouraged to express themselves without fear of failure."What Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is doing today, no one has ever done before. He is unbelievable, a great talent. I don't think I have seen or faced a talent like that," Harbhajan said.The former off-spinner also pointed out how the influence of social media has amplified the visibility of young stars, making their exploits reach a much wider audience than in previous generations."The difference between today's youth and the youth back then is the reach of today's media and social media. Things happened back then too, but today they get highlighted a lot more," he added.Harbhajan also recalled a memorable anecdote involving former India head coach Rahul Dravid that perfectly captured Sooryavanshi's fearless mentality before his IPL debut.According to Harbhajan, Dravid had asked the youngster what he planned to do if he faced a hittable delivery on the very first ball of his IPL career."I think the biggest change is that people are accepting players with that fearless mindset and their approach of playing the way they want to," he said.He continued: "Rahul Dravid was the coach of that team ( Rajasthan Royals ), and he asked Sooryavanshi, 'What will you do on the first ball?' He said, 'If the first ball is in my arc, I will smash it.' And he actually did. He hit a six off the very first ball he faced in his IPL career, against Shardul Thakur."The story, Harbhajan said, underlined the confidence that has made the teenager one of the brightest young batting talents in Indian cricket Alongside his praise for Sooryavanshi, Harbhajan also reflected on the most valuable lesson of his own career, revealing the advice he received from batting icon Sachin Tendulkar ."The best advice I ever got was from the great Sachin Tendulkar," Harbhajan said.Recalling Tendulkar's words, he said: "Sachin paaji told me, 'There will be many distractions, many things will come your way, but you have to keep your blinders on, so that you can't look left or right, and only look straight ahead. And what lies ahead? Cricket! If you stay on this path, no one in the world can stop you. Whatever you want to become, whatever you want to do, you will earn every kind of respect, honour, and fame, everything, if you keep walking on this path. '"Harbhajan said that same message is what he now passes on to young cricketers beginning their journeys."So, I give the same advice to youngsters: keep your focus on the game. You are who you are because of the game. Don't think that you are bigger than the game. If your attitude isn't right, as much as this game provides, it also knows how to take it back just as quickly," he said.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is an "unbelievable" talent, says Harbhajan Singh. The former India spinner says the teenager is achieving something "no one has ever done before" He also reveals the most valuable advice he ever received from Sachin Tendulkar.

Article Title: ICC ODI rankings: Joe Root re-enters top 10, Rohit Sharma closes gap on Virat Kohli
Article Text:
Joe Root (Image: IANS)

Rohit, Gill and Kohli remain among top 5

ICC Men's ODI Batting Rankings (Top 10)



Rank Player Team Rating Points 1 Daryl Mitchell New Zealand 802 2 Shubman Gill India 801 3 Virat Kohli India 767 4 Rohit Sharma India 758 5 Ibrahim Zadran Afghanistan 712 6 Babar Azam Pakistan 689 7 Harry Tector Ireland 679 8 Joe Root England 674 9 Shai Hope West Indies 672 10 Charith Asalanka Sri Lanka 659

England seal first ODI series win over India since 2018



1st ODI – Edgbaston, Birmingham (14 July)

2nd ODI – Sophia Gardens, Cardiff (16 July)

3rd ODI – Lord's, London (19 July)

England's 2-1 ODI series triumph over India has been rewarded in the latest ICC Men's ODI Batting Rankings, with veteran batter Joe Root returning to the top 10 after a sensational series in which he remained unbeaten throughout.Root, who was named Player of the Series, produced unbeaten scores of 76, 99 and 74 to anchor England's first bilateral ODI series victory over India since 2018. His consistency has lifted him four places to No. 8 in the ICC rankings, marking his return to the top 10 for the first time since 2020.England opener Ben Duckett was another major beneficiary after his record-breaking 141 in the third ODI at Lord's. The left-hander jumped 11 places to joint-19th, with his match-winning knock becoming the highest individual score in a Men's ODI at the iconic venue, according to an ICC media release.Despite India losing the series, several Indian batters made gains in the latest rankings following strong individual performances.Rohit Sharma's magnificent 138 in the Lord's decider helped him reduce the gap on Virat Kohli to just nine rating points. Rohit remains fourth in the ODI batting rankings, while Kohli occupies third. India captain Shubman Gill continues to hold the No. 2 position and is just one rating point behind New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell, who remains the world's top-ranked ODI batter with 802 rating points.Middle-order batter Shreyas Iyer also climbed two places to 13th after scoring a fighting 66 in the second ODI at Cardiff.England clinched the three-match ODI series 2-1, registering their first bilateral ODI series victory over the world's No. 1-ranked side since 2018. After India won the opening game, Harry Brook's men responded with back-to-back victories to seal the series.India began the series with a convincing six-wicket win after chasing down 259. Axar Patel starred with four wickets, while Shubman Gill anchored the chase with an unbeaten 80 to give the visitors a 1-0 lead.England bounced back in Cardiff with a four-wicket victory. Joe Root once again held the innings together with a composed unbeaten 99 as England successfully chased 234 to level the series.The decider turned into a run-fest as England piled up a record-breaking 387/3, the highest ODI total ever recorded at Lord's. Ben Duckett smashed 141, eclipsing Sir Viv Richards' long-standing record for the highest individual ODI score at the venue, while Jacob Bethell contributed a fluent 91 during a mammoth 192-run opening stand.India fought back through Rohit Sharma's brilliant 138 off 110 balls, but Sam Curran's four-wicket haul and timely breakthroughs halted the chase as England secured a 27-run victory and the series.
Article Summary: England's 2-1 ODI series triumph over India rewarded in ICC rankings. Joe Root returns to top 10 after sensational series in which he remained unbeaten. Virat Kohli, Shubman Gill and Rohit Sharma remain among top 5.

Article Title: 'I sent a message to Alexis': Mac Allister's father reveals what son told him about Messi's dressing-room pep talks
Article Text:
Argentina's Lionel Messi reacts after losing to Spain in the World Cup final. (AP Photo)

ALSO READ:

'I asked Alexis what had happened'



Messi's message was purely tactical



Argentina's Alexis Mac Allister (20) reacts after Spain's Ferran Torres scored the goal. (AP Photo)

Scaloni also dismisses speculation



The mystery surrounding Lionel Messi 's viral dressing-room speech before Argentina's 2026 FIFA World Cup final has finally been addressed, with Alexis Mac Allister's father dismissing speculation of an internal crisis and insisting the captain's words were taken completely out of context.Carlos Mac Allister revealed that even he briefly wondered whether something had gone wrong inside the Argentina camp after watching footage of Messi repeatedly telling his teammates to "forget everything" before the final against Spain.The clip quickly spread across social media, fuelling theories that Argentina's squad was dealing with tensions behind the scenes before suffering a 0-1 extra-time defeat in New Jersey.However, according to Carlos, there was nothing sinister about Messi's message.According to La Nación’s report, Carlos admitted the video initially left him puzzled."I sent a message to Alexis asking him: what happened in the dressing room? Did something happen? If I had started to wonder, then imagine what others thought," he said.The speculation stemmed from footage released by ESPN showing Messi urging his teammates to stay calm before the biggest match of the tournament."Come on, lads, stay calm. The most important thing is that you stay calm," Messi said.The Argentina captain then added the line that sparked widespread debate."Let's forget everything. Let's just play. Let's focus on the match, lads," Messi added.Those words prompted countless theories online, with many fans interpreting them as evidence that something had happened behind closed doors before kick-off.According to Carlos Mac Allister, the reality was far less dramatic.Carlos said his son immediately dismissed any suggestion of unrest inside the dressing room.Instead, Alexis explained that Messi was simply reminding the players to focus on their football and stick to Argentina's tactical plan."He told me they talked about going out to play in the footballing sense, to keep it on the ground, keep the ball moving, build triangles, and not just lump it forward. That's what they were referring to," Carlos said.He added that the short clip circulating online lacked the surrounding context, making it easy for people to reach incorrect conclusions."Since then, a lot of doubt has come up over these past few days because of that post that went around, and a lot of people have reached out to me about it," he further added.Carlos insisted there were no arguments, no dressing-room divisions and no internal crisis before the final.The rumours gained further momentum after reports claimed Messi and head coach Lionel Scaloni had disagreed over Argentina's tactical approach.Scaloni, however, rejected those suggestions after the match."I don't look at social media. I don't know anything. I have no idea what you're talking about," the Argentina coach said.When questioned further, he added: "I can't believe what you're asking me. We're going in a completely different direction, guys."Carlos also rejected claims that anything other than Spain's performance decided the World Cup final.According to him, every Argentine player gave everything they had, but Spain simply proved to be the better team on the night.The clarification comes after days of intense speculation generated by Messi's emotional speeches before kick-off and at half-time, with the captain repeatedly urging his teammates to stay calm, show personality and focus only on football.While the viral footage sparked endless theories across social media, Carlos Mac Allister's account offers the clearest explanation yet.
Article Summary: Carlos Mac Allister says his son Alexis immediately dismissed any suggestion of unrest inside the dressing room. Alexis explained that Messi was simply reminding the players to focus on their football and stick to Argentina's tactical plan. Carlos insisted there were no arguments, no dressing-room divisions and no internal crisis before the final.

Article Title: FA charges Southampton coach Tonda Eckert over championship 'spygate' scandal
Article Text:
Southampton's coach Tonda Eckert (AP Photo/Kin Cheung, File)

FA alleges Eckert authorised spying on rival clubs



Club continues to back Eckert



Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has been formally charged with misconduct by the English Football Association (FA) over his alleged involvement in the spying scandal that rocked English football during the 2025-26 Championship season. Saints were kicked out of the Championship play-offs in May after admitting they spied on three clubs during the campaign.The FA announced on Wednesday that Eckert faces three alleged breaches of FA Rule E3.1, accusing him of acting in an improper manner and bringing the game into disrepute by authorising the surveillance of opposition training sessions.The FA alleged that Eckert acted in an "improper manner and/or brought the game into disrepute" by authorising the surveillance of opponents' training sessions.The controversy began after the English Football League (EFL) charged Southampton with the unauthorised filming of Middlesbrough's training sessions ahead of their two-legged Championship playoff semifinal, which Southampton won to reach the promotion decider.However, Southampton was later expelled from the playoff final after admitting it had also spied on Oxford United and Ipswich Town earlier in the season.The EFL also handed the club a four-point deduction for the start of the 2026-27 Championship campaign. As a result, Middlesbrough was reinstated in the final but lost 1-0 to Hull City.An independent arbitration panel described the operation as "a contrived and determined plan from top down to gain a competitive advantage." The panel also found that analysts involved in the surveillance "felt pressurised to do the observations that Mr. Eckert and the senior coaches wished them to do."Southampton's expulsion from the playoffs also cost the club the opportunity to earn promotion to the Premier League, along with an estimated $270 million in future revenue.Despite the controversy Southampton said it was sticking by its coach.“As a board, we are fully behind him, and together we only have one objective, we want promotion back to (the) Premier League,'' owner Dragan Solak said in June.The club added: "Tonda and the club will continue to co-operate fully and openly with the FA."Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026-27 Championship season. The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League."We are unable to comment further while the process remains ongoing, but we will provide an update to supporters as soon as we are in a position to do so"Eckert also said in June that he had “made a mistake” and took “full responsibility.”"I am responsible and I apologise for bad judgement; we've be in now for a week and there comes a point to look forward and from the first day back in, there's been lots of smiles and a good energy in the place again," Eckart told to BBC sport.The Southampton coach has until July 28 to submit his official response to the FA's misconduct charges.
Article Summary: Southampton coach Tonda Eckert charged with misconduct by English Football Association. Eckert accused of acting in an improper manner and bringing the game into disrepute. Saints kicked out of Championship play-offs in May after admitting they spied on three clubs.

Article Title: 'I would have headbutted him!': Zlatan Ibrahimovic blasts Leandro Paredes, asks why Spain players just stood and watched
Article Text:
Spain's Gavi, left, falls as he scuffles with Argentina's Leandro Paredes (5) and Thiago Almada. (AP Photo)

'I would have headbutted him'



Zlatan questions Spain's lack of response



ALSO READ:

Zlatan Ibrahimovic (AP Photo)

FIFA investigating Paredes' conduct



Former Sweden striker Zlatan Ibrahimovic has launched a scathing attack on Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes over the ugly scenes that unfolded after the FIFA World Cup final, saying he would have "headbutted" the midfielder had he been on the pitch and accusing Spain's players of failing to stand up for their teammates.The dramatic showdown in New Jersey ended with Spain lifting the World Cup trophy thanks to Ferran Torres' extra-time winner in the 106th minute. However, the celebrations were overshadowed by chaotic post-match confrontations involving several Argentine players and members of the coaching staff.Speaking during his punditry role with Fox Sports, Ibrahimovic did not hold back in his assessment of Paredes' actions, branding the midfielder's behaviour "unprofessional" while expressing disbelief at Spain's passive reaction.Tempers flared after the final whistle as emotions boiled over following Argentina's defeat. The heated exchanges came after Enzo Fernandez had already been sent off late in normal time, with frustration spilling into a post-match melee.Broadcast footage showed Nahuel Molina striking Rodri, while Paredes appeared to kick Eric Garcia before grabbing Gavi by the throat and dragging the Barcelona midfielder to the ground.Roberto Ayala, a member of Argentina's coaching staff, also appeared to become involved during the confrontation as players and officials from both teams rushed in to separate those involved.Reacting to the scenes, Ibrahimovic singled out Paredes for criticism."Paredes can be happy there was no player like me on the pitch. If I had been there, I would have headbutted him and been sent off. It is unprofessional behaviour from him," he said.The former AC Milan, Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United striker has built a reputation for outspoken opinions throughout his career, and his comments after the World Cup final were among his strongest during the tournament.While Paredes was the main target of Ibrahimovic's criticism, the Swedish icon was equally surprised by the reaction of Spain's players, believing they should have done more to defend their teammates during the confrontation."I don't know what the Spanish players are doing? They are just watching another player hit their team-mate," Ibrahimovic said.The chaotic scenes capped an emotionally charged contest in which Spain largely controlled proceedings before Ferran Torres settled the final in extra time. Argentina had struggled to create meaningful chances throughout the match and saw their frustrations boil over as the final whistle approached.Although many expected Paredes to receive a red card for his role in the post-match confrontation, reports later suggested that no dismissal was officially issued during the incident.However, the midfielder may still face retrospective disciplinary action, with FIFA opening an investigation into the events that unfolded after the final whistle.Paredes has since broken his silence on social media but stopped short of addressing the altercation. Instead, he thanked Argentina's supporters and expressed pride in representing his country despite the heartbreaking defeat."Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves—but with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again," he wrote.
Article Summary: Zlatan Ibrahimovic launches scathing attack on Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes. Swede says he would have "headbutted" the midfielder had he been on the pitch. Ibrahimovic also questions Spain's lack of response to post-match melee.

Article Title: Donald Trump wants FIFA chief Gianni Infantino as next UN secretary-general: Report
Article Text:
Donald Trump and FIFA chief Gianni Infantino (AP Photo)

Trump backs Infantino for top UN role

Trump and Infantino grew closer during the World Cup

World Cup final drew boos for Trump and Infantino

Relationship under scrutiny

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe Gianni Infantino would make a good UN Secretary-General? Yes No Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: US President Donald Trump wants FIFA president Gianni Infantino to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations, according to a report by the New York Post.The report said Trump was impressed by Infantino's role in organising the FIFA World Cup and believes the Swiss official has the ability to unite people across the world.According to the report, Trump believes Infantino would be a strong candidate to replace current UN secretary-general António Guterres, whose term ends in December.A source close to Trump told the New York Post: "He is respected by everyone around the world, and recognizes he has a special ability to bring people together."However, it is still unclear whether Infantino is interested in the position or whether Trump has discussed the proposal with him.To become the next UN secretary-general, a candidate must first receive the backing of the 15-member UN Security Council, where the five permanent members have veto power, before being approved by the UN General Assembly.The report said Infantino and Trump developed a close relationship while working together during this year's FIFA World Cup.Infantino reportedly made special efforts to include Trump during the tournament and had earlier presented him with FIFA's inaugural Peace Prize in December.Trump and Infantino were also in the spotlight during the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina.Trump arrived at the stadium aboard Marine One and watched the match from a VIP suite alongside Infantino. According to The Guardian, he received scattered boos when he appeared on the stadium's giant screens before kick-off.The reaction became louder after the match when Trump and Infantino walked onto the field for the trophy presentation following Spain's 1-0 victory.The atmosphere turned more awkward when Trump remained on the podium after handing over the trophy, appearing to join Spain's celebrations before eventually leaving the stage.Trump's close relationship with Infantino also came under scrutiny earlier in the tournament after USA forward Folarin Balogun's one-match suspension for a red card was lifted ahead of the Round of 16 clash against Belgium.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump wants FIFA president Gianni Infantino to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations, according to a report by the New York Post. The report said Trump was impressed byInfantino's role in organising the FIFA World Cup and believes the Swiss official has the ability to unite people across the world. It is still unclear whether Infantinos is interested in the position or whether Trump has discussed the proposal with him.

Article Title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino asked to resign after being accused of 'destroying the football industry'
Article Text:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

Fans' group joins criticism

La Liga president Javier Tebas has once again criticised FIFA president Gianni Infantino, saying he should step down over decisions that he believes are harming football.Tebas accused FIFA of putting commercial interests ahead of the sport by expanding international tournaments and increasing fixture congestion.His latest comments come amid discussions about expanding the 2030 World Cup from 48 to 64 teams.Tebas said expanding the World Cup further would damage domestic competitions, which he believes are the backbone of football.“Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense. The football industry isn't just the World Cup, which is the most important event. But not everything can revolve around the World Cup,” he told Italian outlet La Gazzetta dello Sport, as quoted by news agency AP.He also called for Infantino to leave office, saying, “In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up.”Tebas added that many people privately oppose Infantino but fail to act, claiming: “He shouldn't stay, but he won't leave... those who stay silent are perfectly aware of the damage football is suffering.”Tebas also criticised FIFA's hydration breaks and the extended 27-minute halftime during the World Cup final, saying: “Hydration breaks are a lie...It was a lie — and just a break for advertising.”Football Supporters Europe (FSE) also condemned FIFA's handling of the World Cup, calling for major governance reforms.The group accused FIFA of prioritising commercial interests over supporters, pointing to high ticket prices, expensive travel, poor communication and changes to football traditions.FSE argued that the tournament damaged the reputation of both FIFA and the World Cup, concluding that “FIFA is unfit to govern global football” and accusing Infantino of putting financial and political interests ahead of the game's future.

Article Title: How did Travis Kelce's relationship with Taylor Swift turn the entire Kelce family into global superstars?

Article Title: Nolan Wells case: Stephen A. Smith demands answers after funeral, says "we need to find out what happened"
Article Text:
Nolan Wells case (Via Reddit)

What did Stephen A. Smith say about Nolan Wells?

What did Nolan Wells' independent autopsy reveal?

Eighteen-year-old Nolan Wells was buried on Monday, July 20, more than two weeks after he disappeared during a Fourth of July boating trip off the Mississippi coast. His body was later recovered near Horn Island, but the circumstances surrounding his death remain unanswered. Now, ESPN's Stephen A. Smith is publicly calling for accountability, joining a growing chorus of civil rights leaders and prominent figures demanding a thorough, transparent investigation.Smith used X to address his 6.1 million followers shortly after Wells' funeral concluded on Monday. The message was direct."This is a very sad day," Smith wrote. "Nolan Wells was laid to rest today. My heart goes out to his family and loved ones. But it ain't over. We need to find out what happened to that young man."Smith's platform amplifies something the Wells family has been saying for weeks. Nolan was the only Black member of his friend group on that trip. He was the only one who didn't come home. Those facts have not gone unnoticed, and they've fueled mounting concern that race may have played a role in how the case has been handled.Former San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick, who has long been vocal on racial justice issues, stepped in to fund an independent autopsy.Attorney Ben Crump, who has represented high-profile civil rights cases across the country, flagged serious trust issues with how Mississippi authorities were managing the investigation.At Wells' memorial, Rev. Al Sharpton addressed the grief head-on. "For an 18-year-old young man to no longer be with us, we want answers, not bias either way: just answers," he said. "I think that for the family, the closure can come if there is justice."Wells' mother, Christine Wells-Wonsley, spoke with quiet devastation. "Share his stories, and never stop saying his name," she said. "As long as we continue to remember him, his light will continue to shine through us all."The results, announced Wednesday at an NAACP press conference in Chicago, offered little clarity. Attorney Ben Crump confirmed that the independent autopsy performed by Dr. Roger Mitchell returned inconclusive findings."These findings are inconclusive... pending further investigation," Crump said. "This pathologist cannot rule out if any intervening non-accidental factors contributed to or caused the death of Nolan Wells."Crump acknowledged the body's condition prevented a complete forensic review. The official state autopsy is still pending, and Jackson County Sheriff's Office has not released a cause of death.Wells-Wonsley expressed open frustration with the pace of the official investigation. "The only question we have is what happened to our son?" she said. "Us having the preliminary autopsy results and hearing nothing from them is heartbreaking and concerning." She added that local law enforcement appeared to prematurely label her son's death accidental, a narrative that has already shaped public perception. "Damage has already been done because that's the narrative that's being pushed by the general public," she said.NAACP President Derrick Johnson accused investigators of being "derelict in their duties." The organization has formally urged the U.S. Department of Justice to conduct an independent and transparent review of the events surrounding Wells' death.Wells played football at Ocean Springs High School and Southwest Mississippi Community College. He was remembered by those who loved him as a devoted son, brother, friend and teammate.
Article Summary: Nolan Wells, 18, disappeared during a Fourth of July boating trip off the Mississippi coast. His body was later recovered near Horn Island, but the circumstances surrounding his death remain unanswered. Now, ESPN's Stephen A. Smith is publicly calling for accountability.

Why this photo doesn't add up



A photo claiming to show Cardi B and Nigerian goalkeeper Maduka Okoye kissing on a balcony during Paris Fashion Week has been racking up views online, but there's a problem. It never happened. As the rumor mill around these two keeps spinning, this is one claim that doesn't hold up once you look at what actually went down that day.The image, shared by an account with no real entertainment credentials, shows Cardi and Okoye locked in an embrace with the caption claiming it was taken on a balcony during Paris Fashion Week.It's racked up millions of views and thousands of shares, feeding right into weeks of speculation about the pair after they were first spotted together at the Jean Paul Gaultier Haute Couture show, then again over drinks in Venice.But actual footage and photos from that day, captured by legitimate outlets and photo agencies covering the event, tell a very different story. Every credible report of the balcony moment describes Cardi and Okoye laughing, chatting, and sharing drinks with a group, never kissing or embracing. If a real kiss had actually happened, it would've been the story of the summer, and every outlet already hungry for scraps of this saga would've run with it immediately.None did.Beyond the total absence of this moment from any real coverage, the image itself raises questions.It has the polished, almost too-perfect composition often seen in AI-generated or digitally altered images that get created specifically to cash in on a trending rumor. None of the major photo agencies that actually covered Paris Fashion Week.The ones responsible for the real balcony photos everyone's been circulating have nothing matching this image in their archives. It's a reminder of how fast fabricated content can spread once a celebrity romance rumor picks up steam; people start manufacturing "proof" to keep the story alive, and it often works, racking up views before anyone stops to check.The real story here is dramatic enough without embellishment: Cardi and Okoye have now been seen together multiple times across two countries, all while Okoye's baby mama is publicly airing accusations of abuse and neglect against him. That's plenty to fuel speculation on its own, no fake kiss required.

Article Title: "You don't understand budgets": Pat McAfee responds to ESPN layoff backlash as fans blame his reported $65M deal
Article Text:
"Pat McAfee Brushes Off ESPN Layoff Backlash (Image via Getty)

Pat McAfee brushes off ESPN Layoff backlash again and fans aren't buying it

https://twitter.com/MLFootball/status/2079745993638092829

The real issue: optics don't care about spreadsheets

Pat McAfee is once again the internet's favorite scapegoat, and once again, he's saying it's not fair. ESPN just wrapped up a brutal round of layoffs, showing the door to names fans have watched for years. Ryan Clark, Cam Newton, Karl Ravech, Tom Pelissero, and more. The timing couldn't have been worse for McAfee. Just weeks earlier, reports surfaced that he's negotiating a new deal worth up to $65 million a year, more than double what he currently makes. Social media did the math instantly, and the verdict was brutal: McAfee's bag, their jobs. He addressed it head-on this week, but his explanation didn't land the way he hoped.The numbers tell an ugly story on paper. McAfee reportedly earns around $30 million a year right now, with ESPN in talks to push that to $60-65 million. Meanwhile, Ryan Clark, one of the most recognizable names just shown the door, was reportedly making a fraction of that. Add in Cam Newton, Karl Ravech (33 years at the network), and several others, and it's easy to see why fans connected the dots. JJ Watt even poked fun at it live on McAfee's own show, joking about whether "everybody" got fired just to pay him.McAfee's response leaned on the "you don't get how corporate budgets work" defense, insisting the layoffs and his contract are two separate decisions at a company with "billions and billions of dollars." He even noted this isn't new for him: the same thing happened the first time he signed with ESPN back in 2023, when names like Suzy Kolber and Todd McShay were let go around the same time.McAfee might be technically right that his salary isn't a literal line-item swap for someone else's job. But that argument doesn't actually kill the frustration, it just explains it away. Fans aren't mad about accounting mechanics. They're mad about a company that claims it can't afford loyal, decade-plus veterans while simultaneously fighting to hand one guy a $65 million paycheck. The math might not be mathing for a lot and they are not afraid to call it out.That's not a budgeting error, that's a value statement. And "I feel like you don't fully understand budgets" is not exactly the empathetic answer that was needed in this moment, especially with Ryan Clark finding out he was axed mid-broadcast.The pattern repeating itself 2023, now 2026 is arguably the bigger story here. If this keeps happening every time McAfee's contract comes up, it stops looking like coincidence and starts looking like a trend ESPN needs to actually reckon with, not just wave away as "the narrative."
Article Summary: Pat McAfee is once again the internet's favorite scapegoat, and once again, he's saying it's not fair. ESPN just wrapped up a brutal round of layoffs, showing the door to names fans have watched for years. The timing couldn't have been worse for McAfee. Just weeks earlier, reports surfaced that he's negotiating a new deal worth up to $65 million a year.

Article Title: The Story behind the Champion: "The rent is due every day" Jalen Hurts' remarkable journey from being benched in college to becoming a Super Bowl champion

Jalen Hurts rose to fame at Alabama before encountering his most significant setback

Jalen Hurts’ legacy is more than championships

Every champion has a defining moment, but few have suffered as many public bumps in the road as Jalen Hurts. Long before Hurts became a Super Bowl-winning quarterback for the Philadelphia Eagles, he suffered heartbreak on college football’s biggest stage, heard constant questions about his ability and felt the pressure of having to prove doubters wrong at every level. He wouldn't let adversity get the best of him, he used every challenge as fuel. His journey is one of resilience, discipline, and an unwavering commitment to being the best version of himself.Jalen Hurts came to the University of Alabama in 2016 with much promise but little expectation that he would start as the team’s quarterback as a freshman. Hurts almost immediately won the job under legendary head coach Nick Saban and coached one of the most dominant programs in college football.What a season it was for his debut. Hurts passed for more than 2,700 yards and ran for another 900 as he showed the dual-threat skills that made him one of the nation’s most exciting young quarterbacks. He was named SEC Offensive Player of the Year, and led Alabama to the College Football Playoff National Championship Game.Although Alabama lost a thrilling title game to Clemson, Hurts had already established himself as one of college football’s brightest stars.2017 was another good season but the national championship game against Georgia was a whole different ball game.Hurts started the game, but was pulled at halftime in favor of freshman quarterback Tua Tagovailoa after trailing at the half, in a gutsy decision by Nick Saban. It worked.
